about: Every case where src/core deliberately differs from period-close/. Keyed by test name. Each is a Python behaviour that is wrong by the importer's own promise; none was copied and none was fixed in Python. tools/period_parity.py fails if a listed case stops differing.

test_amount_nan.input: Southern Card row with Amount nan
test_amount_nan.python: crashes in cents(): ValueError, no review, no fault
test_amount_nan.js: bad_amount stop naming file and row

test_valuation_comma_value.python: fnum() swallows the ValueError and plans a valuation of 0.00, exit 0

test_valuation_impossible_month_end.python: the regex passes; in a one-month run the string falls after the month end, so the row is silently dropped, exit 0; in a range such as 2027-01..2027-02 a 2027-01-32 falls inside and the impossible date is planned

test_valuation_impossible_month_end_in_r.input: valuations.csv Month end 2027-01-32 in a 2027-01..2027-02 run

test_two_equal_repayments_same_day.input: two 3000.00 repayments on one day, two matching bank rows
test_two_equal_repayments_same_day.python: both loan lines take the same mate: loan-pair-T0002 is written twice, X0001 is overwritten, T0003 is never paired
test_two_equal_repayments_same_day.js: each bank row is a mate once

seed33.input: fuzz seed 33: a duplicated repayment line in a loan statement, one bank row
seed33.python: both lines take the one bank row as mate
seed33.js: the second is left unpaired for a person

test_one_point_one_without_valuations.input: 1.1 snapshot with no valuations key plus a loan statement
test_one_point_one_without_valuations.python: crashes: len(None) at the Valuations append
test_one_point_one_without_valuations.js: plan note, nothing written for valuations. allow_v1 path only

test_override_missing_column.input: overrides.csv without Category ID or Person

test_policy_impossible_date.python: crashes: ValueError in long_date, escaping the needs-a-person path

test_oversize_field.input: an unterminated quote swallowing over 131072 characters

test_nul_byte.input: a NUL byte in a CSV
test_nul_byte.python: below 3.11 crashes: _csv.Error; 3.11 and later keeps the NUL in the description

test_reversed_month_range.js: PeriodInputError, a host bug and no plan

test_amount_zero.python: -0.0 reaches the review line as (-0.00); the sheet value is the same
test_amount_zero.js: (+0.00): integer cents have no negative zero

test_amount_blank.python: money() reads a blank as 0.0, so a truncated file plans a 0.00 row, exit 0
test_amount_blank.js: bad_amount stop: a blank cell cannot establish an amount; an explicit 0.00 stays valid

test_amount_space.python: money() reads a blank as 0.0, so a truncated file plans a 0.00 row, exit 0
test_amount_space.js: bad_amount stop: a blank cell cannot establish an amount; an explicit 0.00 stays valid

test_leading_apostrophe_formula.python: writes the text unescaped, so USER_ENTERED consumes the source's own apostrophe: '=X lands as =X, the same cell as a real =X, and a re-import plans a second entry
test_leading_apostrophe_formula.js: doubles the leading apostrophe, so the cell keeps the source's text and a re-import finds it

test_leading_apostrophe_word.python: writes the text unescaped, so USER_ENTERED consumes the source's own apostrophe: '=X lands as =X, the same cell as a real =X, and a re-import plans a second entry
test_leading_apostrophe_word.js: doubles the leading apostrophe, so the cell keeps the source's text and a re-import finds it

test_formula_like_text.python: writes the text unescaped, so USER_ENTERED consumes the source's own apostrophe: '=X lands as =X, the same cell as a real =X, and a re-import plans a second entry
test_formula_like_text.js: doubles the leading apostrophe, so the cell keeps the source's text and a re-import finds it

test_amount_huge.js: bad_amount stop: past safe-integer cents, by contract

test_non_ascii_digits.python: reads it, as \d and int() take any Unicode digit
test_non_ascii_digits.js: bad_date stop: ASCII digits only, no shape delivers others

matched, worth a decision: A closing balance from a file exported mid-day holds a run when a later file brings more rows for that day: the ledger counts the whole day. Fails safe, in both.
not compared by the harness: A stray file beside the account folders is silently ignored by Python, against its 'nothing is skipped silently' promise. The core stops on it (file_outside_download_folder); the parity runner drops such files to match the walk, so this is a unit test, not a parity case.
A number in a verify.py MISMATCH line prints as a Python float when the planned cell is a number; JSON cannot tell 51 from 51.0 once parsed.
